module.title: Bridge to A2: Comprehensive Conversational Fluency
module.objective: Integrate past events, present habits, and future plans seamlessly into cohesive everyday conversations as a bridge to A2.

subModules.title: Reading Mission: A Complete Story Across Time
subModules.theme: Past Experiences, Present Feelings, and Future Plans
subModules.grammarFocus: Simple Past, Present Simple and Continuous, and be going to with connectors
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Travel experiences, feelings, plans, and time connectors

content.summary: In this reading mission, you will follow a short personal story from the past to the present and the future. You will read about a finished trip, how a person feels now, and plans for tomorrow. Notice how connectors such as because, so, but, then, and after that make the story clear and natural. This is an important step toward A2 because you can understand a complete conversation, not only separate sentences.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Use the Simple Past for finished actions, the present for now, and be going to for future plans. Connect ideas with because, so, but, then, and after that.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Travel, activities, feelings, preparation, recommendations, schedules, and experiences.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: First, skim the passage to find the main story. Next, scan for time words such as yesterday, now, tomorrow, then, and after that to find key details.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a short passage about a past trip, present feelings, and future plans.
Identify key details such as places, activities, reasons, and plans.
Recognize Simple Past, present forms, and be going to in one connected story.
Use time connectors to follow the order of events.

contextWarmup.prompt: Which sentence tells a complete story from the past to the future?
options: I visited my aunt yesterday, and now I am tired, so I am going to rest tomorrow.
I visit my aunt yesterday and tired tomorrow.
I am going to visited my aunt yesterday.
contextWarmup.explanation: This sentence is clear because it uses visited for the past, am tired for now, and am going to rest for a future plan.

rules: Use the Simple Past for a finished action: I visited the museum yesterday.
Use am, is, or are for feelings and actions now: I am tired now. She is relaxing at home.
Use am, is, or are going to plus a base verb for a future plan: We are going to travel tomorrow.
Use connectors to show reasons, results, contrast, and order: I was tired, so I went home. Then I made dinner.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Jumping Between Times Without Clear Words
commonTrap.explanation: A story can be confusing when it changes from yesterday to now or tomorrow without a connector or the correct verb form. Look for time words and check the verb after each subject.
commonTrap.wrong: I go to the beach yesterday. I tired now. I sleep tomorrow.
commonTrap.correct: I went to the beach yesterday. I am tired now, so I am going to sleep early tomorrow.

content.contractionsTitle: Natural Spoken Contractions: Talking About Time
content.contractionsSubtitle: Observe how subjects and verbs smoothly merge in natural spoken English:

contractions.subject: You
contractions.exampleFull: You are going to enjoy the trip.
contractions.exampleContracted: You're going to enjoy the trip.

contractions.subject: We
contractions.exampleFull: We are going to explore the town.
contractions.exampleContracted: We're going to explore the town.

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Structure with Past, Present, and Future Time
grammarFormulas.description: Assemble and swap sentence blocks to explore affirmative, negative, and question patterns:
complements: are preparing for a busy week
am going to call my friend tomorrow
are going to explore the market after lunch

items.collocation: I am exhausted after the long trip.
The view from the hill was amazing.
We are going to relax at home tonight.
They explored the old town yesterday.
I am preparing for my trip tomorrow.
The festival was a wonderful experience.
We decided to stay until Sunday.
My friend recommended this small café.
My schedule is busy this week.
After that, we walked to the station.

content.context: Maya tells her friend about her weekend, how she feels today, and her plan for tomorrow.
content.text: Last Saturday, Maya visited her cousin Lina in a small town near the sea. They explored the old market and bought fresh fruit. Then they walked to the beach because the weather was sunny. The view was amazing, so Maya took many photos. After that, they ate fish at a little restaurant that Lina recommended. Maya returned home late, and she was exhausted. Now it is Monday morning. Maya is at home and she is preparing for her English class. She feels tired, but she is happy because the weekend was a wonderful experience. Her schedule is busy today, so she is drinking tea and doing her homework slowly. Tomorrow, Maya is going to meet Lina again. They are going to plan a short trip for next month.

highlights.note: Visited is the Simple Past form of visit. It tells us about a finished action last Saturday.
Because gives a reason: they walked to the beach because the weather was sunny.
Is preparing describes an action happening now.
Are going to plus a base verb describes a future plan.

gistQuestion.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Maya talks about her past weekend, her feelings now, and a future plan.
Maya learns to cook fish at a restaurant.
Maya has an English class at the beach.
gistQuestion.explanation: The passage moves from Maya's Saturday trip to her Monday morning and then to her plan for tomorrow.

detailQuestions.prompt: Where did Maya and Lina go after the old market?
detailQuestions.explanation: They walked to the beach because the weather was sunny.

detailQuestions.prompt: Why did Maya take many photos?
options: Lina asked her to take photos.
detailQuestions.explanation: The text says that the view was amazing, so Maya took many photos.

detailQuestions.prompt: How does Maya feel on Monday morning?
detailQuestions.explanation: Maya feels tired because she returned home late, but she is happy about her weekend.

detailQuestions.prompt: What are Maya and Lina going to do tomorrow?
options: Plan a short trip for next month.
detailQuestions.explanation: Tomorrow, they are going to meet and plan a short trip for next month.

questions.question: When did Maya visit Lina?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says that Maya visited her cousin Lina last Saturday.

questions.question: Which word in the passage shows the reason for walking to the beach?
questions.explanation: Because introduces a reason. They walked to the beach because the weather was sunny.

questions.question: What did Maya and Lina eat at the restaurant?
questions.explanation: They bought fresh fruit at the market, but they ate fish at the restaurant.

questions.question: Which sentence is about Maya's present action?
options: She is preparing for her English class.
She is going to meet Lina.
questions.explanation: Is preparing shows an action happening now. Visited is past, and is going to meet is a future plan.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly describes Maya's future plan?
options: Maya and Lina are going to plan a trip.
Maya and Lina planned a trip yesterday.
Maya and Lina are planning a trip last Saturday.
questions.explanation: Are going to plan is the correct form for a future plan. The passage says they will plan a short trip for next month.

subModules.title: Listening Mission: Past, Present, and Future Plans

content.summary: In this listening mission, two friends meet after a holiday. Listen for time words to understand the order of events. They talk about the past, their feelings now, and plans for the future. Listen for past verbs such as "went" and "visited", present phrases such as "I am tired", and future plans with "going to".
learningObjectives: Identify past activities in a short conversation.
Understand how speakers feel in the present.
Recognise future plans with "be going to".
Follow a conversation that moves from the past to the present and the future.

keyPhrases.note: Use this question to ask about a holiday that has finished.
Use "went" to talk about a finished trip in the past.
Use this phrase to describe how you feel now.

keyPhrases.phrase: What are you going to do this weekend?
keyPhrases.meaning: Apa yang akan kamu lakukan akhir pekan ini?
keyPhrases.note: Use this question to ask about a future plan.

keyPhrases.phrase: I am going to stay at home.
keyPhrases.note: Use "am going to" before a planned future action.
Use "can" to suggest a possible plan.

connectedSpeech.note: In natural speech, "was" is often weak and sounds like "wuz". The words join together smoothly.

connectedSpeech.slow: I am going to stay at home.
connectedSpeech.slowIpa: /aɪ æm ˈɡəʊɪŋ tuː steɪ æt həʊm/
connectedSpeech.note: In quick informal speech, "I am" becomes "I'm" and "going to" can sound like "gonna".
The final sound in "about" can join the "y" sound in "you", making a soft "ch" sound.

sections.title: Audio Dialogue: Meeting After the Holiday

content.context: Lisa and Tom meet after a long holiday. They talk about Tom's trip last week, how he feels now, and their plans for next week.
content.audioPrompt: Listen carefully to the following dialogue between Lisa and Tom. Notice the past, present, and future time expressions.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: Hi Tom! How was your holiday? I didn't see you last week.
lines.translation: Hai Tom! Bagaimana liburanmu? Aku tidak melihatmu minggu lalu.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It was amazing! I went to Yogyakarta with my family. We visited Borobudur and also explored the old city.
lines.translation: Luar biasa! Aku pergi ke Yogyakarta dengan keluargaku. Kami mengunjungi Borobudur dan juga menjelajahi kota tua.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: That sounds wonderful! How do you feel now? Are you tired?
lines.translation: Kedengarannya menyenangkan! Bagaimana perasaanmu sekarang? Apakah kamu lelah?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Yes, I'm a bit exhausted because we walked a lot. But I'm happy and relaxed.
lines.translation: Ya, aku sedikit kelelahan karena kami banyak berjalan. Tapi aku senang dan santai.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: I understand. So, what are you going to do this weekend? Any plans?
lines.translation: Aku mengerti. Jadi, apa yang akan kamu lakukan akhir pekan ini? Ada rencana?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I'm going to stay at home and rest. After that, I'm going to prepare for my presentation next Monday. How about you?
lines.translation: Aku akan tinggal di rumah dan beristirahat. Setelah itu, aku akan mempersiapkan presentasiku Senin depan. Bagaimana denganmu?

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: I stayed in Jakarta last week, but I'm going to visit my grandparents this Sunday. I miss them.
lines.translation: Aku tinggal di Jakarta minggu lalu, tapi aku akan mengunjungi kakek nenekku Minggu ini. Aku rindu mereka.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's nice! Enjoy your time with them. Then we can meet next week and have coffee together.
lines.translation: Bagus sekali! Nikmati waktumu dengan mereka. Lalu kita bisa bertemu minggu depan dan minum kopi bersama.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Tell Your Story Across Time

content.summary: Write a short conversation or paragraph about the past, the present, and the future. Start with a finished past activity, say how you feel or what you are doing now, and finish with a future plan. Use connectors to make your ideas clear.

blueprintItems.title: Start with a Past Experience
blueprintItems.example: I visited my grandmother last Sunday.

blueprintItems.title: Add a Past Detail
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + was/were + adjective, or Subject + Verb 2 + detail.
blueprintItems.example: The weather was sunny, so we walked in the park.

blueprintItems.title: Talk About Now
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + present verb, or Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing.
blueprintItems.example: Now I feel happy and I am resting at home.

blueprintItems.title: Finish with a Future Plan
blueprintItems.example: Next weekend, I am going to visit her again.

blueprintItems.title: Connect Your Ideas
blueprintItems.example: I was tired, but I am going to study tonight.

mechanicsRules.rule: Start every sentence with a capital letter.
mechanicsRules.why: The first word in a sentence and the word I need capital letters.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use a full stop at the end of a statement.
mechanicsRules.badExample: I am going to call my friend
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I am going to call my friend.
mechanicsRules.why: A full stop shows that your sentence is finished.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use the correct time verb form.
mechanicsRules.why: Use Verb 2 for a finished activity in the past.

mechanicsRules.rule: Write am, is, or are before going to.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I am going to cook dinner.
mechanicsRules.why: Use am, is, or are with going to for a future plan.

sampleSentences.en: Last Saturday, I played football with my friends.
It was exciting, but I was very tired after the game.
sampleSentences.id: A past feeling with was and a contrast connector.

sampleSentences.en: Now I am relaxing at home because my legs hurt.
sampleSentences.id: A present activity and a reason.

sampleSentences.en: Tomorrow, I am going to watch a football match on TV.
sampleSentences.id: A future plan with going to.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: last week i visit my cousin
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Last week I visited my cousin.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Minggu lalu saya mengunjungi sepupu saya.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use a capital letter at the start, write I with a capital letter, use Verb 2 for the past, and add a full stop.

mechanicsChallenges.translation: Sekarang dia sedang memasak makan malam.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use is before a verb ending in -ing for an activity happening now.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: tomorrow we going to go to the beach
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: Tomorrow we are going to go to the beach.
mechanicsChallenges.translation: Besok kami akan pergi ke pantai.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use are before going to when the subject is we.

mechanicsChallenges.faultySentence: i was tired so i go home
mechanicsChallenges.targetSentence: I was tired, so I went home.
mechanicsChallenges.keyRule: Use a comma before so when it joins two ideas. Use went for a finished past action.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 1: My Day Then and Now
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write 3 or 4 sentences. Write about one thing you did yesterday. Then write how you feel or what you are doing now. Use yesterday, now, and one connector such as but or so.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Yesterday I cleaned my room. It was very messy, so I worked for one hour. Now I feel tired, but my room is clean.

guidedLabChallenges.title: Challenge 2: Past, Present, and Future
guidedLabChallenges.instruction: Write a short paragraph with 4 or 5 sentences. Include a finished past activity, a present feeling or activity, and a future plan. Use at least two connectors from also, but, because, so, then, or after that.
guidedLabChallenges.example: Last weekend I visited the beach with my family. It was sunny, so we swam in the sea. After that, we ate lunch near the beach. Now I am at home and I feel relaxed. Next month, I am going to go there again.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Write 3 sentences about a meal you had in the past, what you are doing now, and what you are going to eat tomorrow.
practicumQuestions.criteria: Write one correct past sentence, one correct present sentence, and one future sentence with going to. Use capital letters and full stops.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: Yesterday I ate noodles with my sister. Now I am drinking water at home. Tomorrow I am going to cook rice and chicken.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Write a short message to a friend about your weekend. Say what you did, how you feel now, and one plan for next weekend. Use but, because, or so.
practicumQuestions.criteria: Write at least 30 words. Include Simple Past, a present form, and be going to. Use one connector correctly.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: Hi Mia. Last weekend I watched a new film with my brother. It was funny, so we laughed a lot. Now I feel happy because the film was great. Next weekend, I am going to visit you.

practicumQuestions.prompt: Write a 4-sentence mini story about a busy day. Put your ideas in time order with then or after that. Finish with a future plan.
practicumQuestions.criteria: Write four complete sentences. Use a past action, a past detail, a present sentence, and a future plan. Use then or after that correctly.
practicumQuestions.sampleGoodAnswer: Yesterday I went to the market. Then I bought fruit for my family. Now I am making a fruit salad in the kitchen. After dinner, I am going to call my grandmother.

content.summary: In a full conversation, you can talk about the past, the present, and the future. Use clear time words such as last weekend, today, tonight, tomorrow, and next weekend. Connect your ideas with and, but, because, after that, and so.
content.audioGuidance: Speak slowly and clearly. Use a falling voice at the end of complete answers. Use a rising voice for yes or no questions. Stress important words, especially time words, action words, and feeling words.

pillars.name: Clear Time
pillars.explanation: Use past verbs for finished activities: I went to the park. Use present language for now: I feel tired today. Use going to for plans: I am going to watch a movie tonight.

pillars.name: Connected Ideas
pillars.explanation: Use and to add information, but to show a different idea, because to give a reason, and after that to show the next action.

pillars.name: Natural Rhythm
pillars.explanation: Make key words stronger: LAST weekend, I WENT to the PARK. Today I FEEL GOOD, but I am a bit TIRED.

pillars.name: Friendly Intonation
pillars.explanation: Raise your voice for a yes or no question: Are you going to rest? Lower your voice at the end of an answer: Yes, I am going to rest tonight.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: PREsent is a thing you give to someone. PreSENT means to give or show something.
A REcord is saved information, music, or a result. To reCORD means to save sound or video.
A CONtract is a written agreement. To conTRACT means to become smaller.

drills.focus: Rising intonation in a yes or no question
drills.hint: Let your voice rise gently on weekend.

roleplay.context: You are having a friendly conversation with Mr. Khoirul. Talk about your activities last weekend, your feelings today, and your plans for tonight and next weekend.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Hello! I am happy to see you today. What did you do last weekend? Did you go anywhere?
turns.translation: Halo! Saya senang bertemu denganmu hari ini. Apa yang kamu lakukan akhir pekan lalu? Apakah kamu pergi ke suatu tempat?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Hi, Mr. Khoirul! Last weekend, I went to the park with my friends. We played badminton and had a picnic.
turns.translation: Hai, Pak Khoirul! Akhir pekan lalu, saya pergi ke taman bersama teman-teman saya. Kami bermain bulu tangkis dan piknik.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That sounds fun! How was the weather? How do you feel today?
turns.translation: Wah, kedengarannya menyenangkan! Bagaimana cuacanya? Bagaimana perasaanmu hari ini?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: The weather was sunny and nice. Today I feel good, but I am a bit tired because I did not sleep much.
turns.translation: Cuacanya cerah dan bagus. Hari ini saya merasa baik, tetapi saya sedikit lelah karena saya tidak banyak tidur.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: I see. What are you going to do tonight?
turns.translation: Saya mengerti. Apa yang akan kamu lakukan malam ini?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Tonight, I am going to watch a movie at home. After that, I am going to sleep early.
turns.translation: Malam ini, saya akan menonton film di rumah. Setelah itu, saya akan tidur lebih awal.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Good plan! What are you going to do next weekend?
turns.translation: Rencana yang bagus! Apa yang akan kamu lakukan akhir pekan depan?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Next weekend, I am going to visit my cousin. We are going to explore the city and try local food.
turns.translation: Akhir pekan depan, saya akan mengunjungi sepupu saya. Kami akan menjelajahi kota dan mencoba makanan lokal.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Answer the question about your feelings today. Add a reason with because or a contrast with but.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: How do you feel today after your weekend?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Mr. Khoirul asks how you feel now after a busy or relaxing weekend.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student sharing your present feeling and a simple reason.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Today I feel good, but I am a little tired because I did not sleep much.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /təˈdeɪ aɪ fiːl ɡʊd bət aɪ æm ə ˈlɪt.əl ˈtaɪərd bɪˈkɔːz aɪ dɪd nɒt sliːp mʌtʃ/
practicumQuestions.hint: Stress your feeling word, such as happy, good, tired, excited, or busy.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay checks present-time language and your ability to explain a feeling.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Tell Mr. Khoirul about your plan for tonight. Say what you are going to do and what you will do after that.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: What are you going to do tonight?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Mr. Khoirul wants to know how you will relax or prepare for the next day.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student describing a simple plan for tonight.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Tonight, I am going to watch a movie at home. After that, I am going to sleep early.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /təˈnaɪt aɪ æm ˈɡoʊ.ɪŋ tə wɑːtʃ ə ˈmuː.vi æt hoʊm ˈæf.tər ðæt/
practicumQuestions.hint: Say going to smoothly and clearly. Stress TONIGHT and AFTER THAT.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay checks future plans with going to and sequence language.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Answer with a plan for next weekend. Include who you are going with or what you want to do.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: What are you going to do next weekend? Are you going to do something special?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Mr. Khoirul asks about your upcoming weekend and possible special plans.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a student sharing an exciting future plan.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Next weekend, I am going to visit my cousin, and we are going to try local food.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /nekst ˈwiːk.end aɪ æm ˈɡoʊ.ɪŋ tə ˈvɪz.ɪt maɪ ˈkʌz.ɪn ænd wi ɑːr ˈɡoʊ.ɪŋ tə traɪ ˈloʊ.kəl fuːd/
practicumQuestions.hint: Use a happy voice when you talk about an exciting plan.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This roleplay checks if you can make a longer future answer with a connected idea.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the time words in a complete sentence: last weekend, today, tonight, and tomorrow.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Make one short connected sentence with the time words.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Last weekend I was busy, today I am tired, and tomorrow I am going to rest.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /lɑːst ˈwiːk.end aɪ wəz ˈbɪz.i təˈdeɪ aɪ æm ˈtaɪərd ænd təˈmɒr.oʊ aɪ æm ˈɡoʊ.ɪŋ tə rest/
practicumQuestions.hint: Say each time word clearly. These words tell your listener when something happens.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill checks useful vocabulary for talking about different times.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say the three sentences. Use went for the past, feel for the present, and going to for the future.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Repeat: Yesterday I went to school. Today I feel good. Tomorrow I am going to study.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Yesterday I went to school. Today I feel good. Tomorrow I am going to study.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ˈjes.tər.deɪ aɪ went tə skuːl təˈdeɪ aɪ fiːl ɡʊd təˈmɒr.oʊ aɪ æm ˈɡoʊ.ɪŋ tə ˈstʌd.i/
practicumQuestions.hint: Do not say I went tomorrow. Use I am going to for a future plan.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill checks the basic grammar forms for past, present, and future meaning.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say both words and make the strong syllable clear: PREsent, then preSENT.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Listen and repeat: This is a PREsent. I preSENT my work today.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: This is a PREsent. I preSENT my work today.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈprez.ənt aɪ prɪˈzent maɪ wɜːrk təˈdeɪ/
practicumQuestions.hint: For the thing, stress PRE. For the action, stress SENT.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill checks if you can hear and produce a change in syllable stress.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Ask the question with a rising voice. Then answer it with a falling voice.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Repeat: Are you going to visit your cousin this weekend? Yes, I am going to visit my cousin this weekend.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Are you going to visit your cousin this weekend? Yes, I am going to visit my cousin this weekend.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ɑːr ju ˈɡoʊ.ɪŋ tə ˈvɪz.ɪt jʊr ˈkʌz.ɪn ðɪs ˈwiːk.end jes aɪ æm ˈɡoʊ.ɪŋ tə ˈvɪz.ɪt maɪ ˈkʌz.ɪn ðɪs ˈwiːk.end/
practicumQuestions.hint: Let your voice rise at the end of the question. Let it fall at the end of the answer.
practicumQuestions.explanation: This drill checks rising intonation for a yes or no question and falling intonation for a complete answer.
